(2) Create cross-constraints where one agent's hidden fact blocks another team's apparent natural assignment — e.g., make Gate 3 appear available for the network team in public context, so PF3's shielded-route requirement is the only thing that forces Gate 1 instead. (3) Add a decoy gate or time window in the public context that is not actually available, so agents must disclose constraints to eliminate it. (4) Ensure at least two of PF1–PF4 each flip a decision from a wrong-but-plausible public default to the correct answer, so that removing any one fact produces a measurably wrong settlement. No changes to check IDs C1–C8, P1–P2, or fact IDs PF1–PF4 are needed — the checks and facts are correctly designed; the scenario's public context and default-plausible assignments need to be restructured to make the hidden information genuinely decisive.
